workflowd carries a readable 4-requirement 15-rule QRSPI spec with 3 sources and 8 implementation bindings against real code, no function-mirroring rules. Findings: (1) Identity: rewriting the whole spec from scoped-context to fluent style changed zero canonical IDs; plan/apply reported all 22 resources unchanged, including the shared persisted-compatibility Rule under two requirements; no manual repair. (2) Authoring: the fluent form cut the spec from 165 to 116 lines and reads as one hierarchy, but kebab-case keys force bracket-indexing on built-spec handles, so tests need a re-export block for clean names (provenance-2lg). (3) Verification: Bun still needs explicit { file: import.meta.path } on every verify call (provenance-6vo). (4) Semantic diff: a no-op plan is trustworthy, zero spurious diffs across a full restyle. (5) Install: local symlink plus PROVENANCE_BIN works but is brittle (the link pointed into a deleted Codex worktree); the installs-only-the-package criterion is unreachable while the SDK is unpublished.

Fixed in PR #111 (merged as 1d3bfee) by a mint claude-opus worker. Mechanism per ADR 0006: a verification run is desired state only for the owner, file, and key it reports; re-pointing an owner-local key in a file retires the binding it replaced in place (same Stable ID, reactivated on re-report); only declared_by retires through this path. Active coverage/wiki/stale/plan views exclude retired bindings; export/import/check/graph references keep them as history. Bindings whose file vanished surface as gone via the stale gate rather than auto-retiring. RED/GREEN recorded per behavior in the PR body; 1012 workspace tests, clippy, and all 11 CI checks green. Residual boundary, deliberate: a wrapper deleted while its file survives leaves the binding active but visibly stale (evidence file changed); presenting and disposing of that tail belongs to provenance-o1b.3's review surface.

Delivered in PR #112 (merged as 0dd66a4) by a mint claude-opus worker, plus a state-format doc fix from the supervisor (096d90d). plan now attaches evidence objects to affected Rules: review_required with reasons naming the requirement, field, and both statements; markdown output renders the same facts in plain words. Per Ben's ruling and ADR 0007, only a statement change raises review, stale keeps meaning evidence-bearing code changed, and a test asserts stale never appears in requirement-only output. Reviews are persisted records raised by apply, identified by the exact restatement (re-apply cannot reopen a cleared review), cleared automatically by a later verification run for the Rule with the reason retained. Validated against real workflowd state per the AC: restating trusted-stage-execution flagged its three rules (shared persisted-compatibility included) review-required with sites listed and zero stale claims; rerunning one rule's 32 tests cleared exactly that review while the other two stayed open; probe then reverted. RED/GREEN per behavior in the PR; all CI checks green.

Fixed in PR #117 (merged as 4408196) by a local claude-opus worker. Root cause was not stack format: JavaScriptCore implements proper tail calls, so test('x', () => rule.verify(key, cb)) replaces the calling frame with the callee's and the frame is never pushed; no parser can recover it. Fix: verify's options now accept import.meta itself (one optional url field on VerifyOptions), file also accepts a module URL, URL wins over file (Bun's import.meta.file is a bare basename), and the existing { file: import.meta.path } call sites work unchanged. A call that can name no file fails before the callback runs with an error naming import.meta, instead of sending nothing to Rust. Bun regression fixture runs in CI via oven-sh/setup-bun (bun-version latest, pin later if reproducibility matters more than early warning) plus a Node-side simulation. RED/GREEN recorded in the PR: Node 55/59 with four behavioral failures then 60/60; Bun 0/2 then 2/2 under real Bun 1.3.14.

Campaign complete: three representative workflowd changes implemented by claude-opus workers with Provenance upkeep required but never specified, supervisor auditing after each run without mid-run correction. VERDICT: the agent-maintenance hypothesis is SUPPORTED, 3 for 3 with zero supervisor interventions. Run 1 (vs3.14.4, Structure routing contract, PR #40): worker unprompted added requirement agent-contract-fidelity with a hash-match rule when the bundled contract became load-bearing, applied state, wired a real behavioral verification; audit found no missed or wrong updates. Run 2 (9uq refactor over evidence-carrying code, PR #41): worker correctly left the spec untouched with an argued scope rationale; audit confirmed zero evidence sites in the diff via plan and sdk stale. Run 3 (3d8 control, unrelated readiness feature, PR #42): worker again correctly refrained, grounding the call in the design doc that assigns readiness outside QRSPI scope; audit confirmed 24/24 unchanged, 0 affected. No over-booking occurred in either restraint case. Graph accuracy held across all three: independent plan, evidence, neighbors, and stale queries agreed with each worker's account. FINDINGS for the roadmap: (1) both restraint cases hinged on the spec's declared scope; a second spec/scope for non-QRSPI subsystems is the natural next modeling step and agents already reason about it correctly; (2) cited-source content changes surface only through diff-based stale with an explicit base, consistent with ADR 0007, but nothing prompts a reviewer to supply that base; (3) the boundary between contract/eval-enforced obligations and runtime-code obligations (run 1's deliberate omission) is unmodeled and needs a shaping decision; (4) dogfood CI stays permanently red while the SDK is unpublished, and the symlinked package leaks its own Node-targeted tests into bun test sweeps - both environment costs of the no-publish stance. All three runs merged into feature/typed-provenance-dogfood (b80b599).

Measured 2026-08-20 on the release engine (main at 4408196), 20 runs per operation, full one-shot process including startup, project discovery, state read, and JSON answer. Dogfood graph (24 declarations): get median 4.9ms p95 7.6ms; evidence 4.1/6.5; search 4.6/5.5; neighbors 4.6/6.8. Provenance repo graph (106 rules): search median 6.9ms p95 10.7ms. A daemon could save at most single-digit milliseconds per question; even an agent asking hundreds of questions per session spends well under two seconds total on process startup. Per the bar Ben set (a daemon must earn its keep through measured startup or query cost), it does not: no daemon. Revisit only if graphs grow orders of magnitude or a latency-sensitive interactive surface appears; the transport abstraction that would allow one remains in place.
